neighbours.label: the bare modifier right after 'in' in an idiomatic 'in + adjective/quantifier + noun' phrase ('in more detail', 'in sufficient time', 'in good condition'), as against 'in' followed by an article
fire: The report explains the new tax rules in greater detail on page four.
Luckily the ambulance arrived in enough time to save the injured climber.
The museum keeps the old manuscripts in perfect condition behind glass.
The village has changed in many ways since the railway closed.
The second chapter covers the treaty in more depth than the first.
After the storm, the roof was still in decent shape according to the builder.
The festival is still celebrated in modern-day towns along the river.
She described the accident to the police in full detail the next morning.
quiet: The report explains the new tax rules with greater care on page four.
Luckily the ambulance arrived at the scene to save the injured climber.
The museum keeps the old manuscripts in a cabinet behind glass.
The village has built more houses since the railway closed.
The second chapter covers the treaty and the war that followed.
After the storm, the roof was still standing according to the builder.
The festival is still celebrated in the towns along the river.
She described the accident to the police at the station the next morning.

predictions: fire 0.5-0.9 on the word after 'in' in article-less phrases; 'in the/a' and 'with more' below 0.25
notes: Card: ' more' x11 after 'in', ' sufficient', ' present', ' some', ' good'. Probe: 'in sufficient time' 0.876, 'In more ways' 0.847, 'in good condition' 0.641, 'in present-day' 0.617, 'in more detail' 0.573; 'with more care' 0.012, 'more detail on' 0.009, 'in the kitchen' 0.098, 'in a small flat' 0.206.
